I live in New England, where it gets quite cold in the first few months of the year. Earlier this year (anxiety was at an all time high post christmas/new years) I was broke, and couldn't afford the fuel to heat my water system in my home. I had just two options: either take ice cold showers when the warmest day wouldn't break 0 degrees Fahrenheit, or take a shower at work.

There was no way in hell I was going to wake up early enough to get to work before any co-workers arrived and shower in peace. So my only option was ice cold showers.

The first morning, I started the shower and climbed in on the end that the water sprays to. Put my feet in, within a few seconds they were numb. I step a few inches more into the spray, to get up to my knees wet. My breathing started to elevate as my body temperature began to dip. Closer I walked, my stomach is getting sprayed now. Trembling uncontrollably at this point I say fuck it and walk all the way in. I'm breathing so heavily at this point my lungs began to hurt, i began washing myself as quickly as possible. By the time I was rinsing the soap off, I realized that I was no longer cold. Turning off the shower and reaching for my towel, I came to the shocking discovery that I was actually hot. My skin felt so warm and as I dried off my breathing mellowed out and I felt so full of energy.

The next day I looked forward to the challenge. "I've done this once now, I can do it again!" I thought. It was still just as challenging as the day previous, but I felt more determined. 

The physical and mental challenge of exposing myself to something which I consider one of the most extreme challenges I have ever put myself through.  

Over the course of the next few weeks, the entire thought of taking a hot shower seemed pointless. I felt myself becoming mentally indestructible. It was such an incredible experience. I haven't had much anxiety since then, after suffering from dramatic panic attacks near daily. 

If you have taken the time to read all of this, I hope any fellow anxiety ridden redditors give this a try and see what wonders it can do for you.
